description:
No spec subject (candidates: specled.severity / CLI output surface when picked up). Severity: Low. From 2026-08-06 critical review of specled_-q0q. The new append_only/self_authorized_weakening marker resolves to :info, and default CLI output does not render :info findings — the always-visible marker the epic shipped is in practice visible only in HTML review output or verbose modes. Keep-reason: CLI output-policy change (how :info renders by default) needs its own small design call; out of scope for the defect branch. Concrete failure: a maintainer running bare mix spec.check on a self-authorizing PR sees a green result with no marker line, defeating the visibility intent.

## ORCHESTRATOR CONTRACT (specled_-i4x)

Advances: specled.mix_tasks

(Orchestrator note: NOT specled.severity — nothing about severity RESOLUTION changes, only
stdout filtering. Not specled.branch_guard unless branch_check.ex is touched, which it should
not be. specled.mix_tasks owns lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex, .spec/specs/mix_tasks.spec.md:22.)

THIS TICKET'S PREMISE IS MATERIALLY OVERSTATED — re-scope before implementing. The
concrete-failure claim ("a maintainer running bare mix spec.check sees a green result with no
marker line") is wrong on the second half. print_branch_report/2
(lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex:252-257) ALWAYS prints the info count plus an explicit visibility
disclosure:

  branch base=... findings=N (error=E warning=W info=I, info hidden; --verbose to show)

That line landed in 134d0e8d (0.8.0), five releases before 0.13.0, and is a spec'd must —
specled.tasks.branch_findings_breakdown (.spec/specs/mix_tasks.spec.md:292-301). What is
genuinely hidden is the marker's DETAIL line (which requirement, which ADR), suppressed by
filter_for_stdout/2 (lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex:216-224). The ticket also says --debug; the
flag is --verbose, plus SPECLED_SHOW_INFO=1 (lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex:207-213).

CORRECT FRAMING: the count is disclosed, the detail is not. The design call is whether specific
:info codes get an always-on carve-out from filter_for_stdout/2.

DECISION-CLASS: yes — spec amendment required. The ticket does NOT self-describe this, and this
is the one most likely to ambush you mid-implementation. specled.tasks.check_verbose_flag
(.spec/specs/mix_tasks.spec.md:185-188) is a must reading "findings whose resolved severity is
:info shall be suppressed from stdout" — UNCONDITIONAL. Any always-visible carve-out contradicts
it verbatim. Because the amendment removes an absolute from a must,
append_only/must_downgraded or scenario_regression may fire and require an authorizing ADR with
change_type: adds-exception, affects: [specled.tasks.check_verbose_flag]. Per operator ruling on
epic specled_-i4x: draft fully, record completion normally; the orchestrator will NOT merge
without human sign-off.

Allowed touches:
- lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex
- .spec/specs/mix_tasks.spec.md
- .spec/decisions/specled.decision.*.md
- test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs
- test/mix/tasks/spec_tasks_test.exs
- .spec/realization_hashes.json  (Mix.Tasks.Spec.Check.run/1 is a tracked api_boundary binding.
  Post-0.14.0 a body edit inside run/1 should NOT move it — hashing is head + arg shapes only,
  lib/specled_ex/realization/api_boundary.ex:51-57 — but it is listed so you are not blocked.)
- docs/concepts.md, README.md  (only if flag semantics are taught there)
- CHANGELOG.md

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex
- lib/specled_ex/branch_check/severity.ex
- lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex
- lib/specled_ex/review/html.ex

Out of Scope (intent):
- Do NOT raise append_only/self_authorized_weakening from :info to :warning. That changes
  exit-status math and defeats "visible but not blocked"
  (lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex:523-540).
- Do NOT change the summary-line format. It is pinned verbatim by a must and by scenario
  specled.tasks.branch_findings_breakdown.summary_and_order.
- Do NOT make --verbose the default. specled.package docs instruct adopters to use --verbose to
  probe for detector_unavailable (.spec/specs/package.spec.md:26-29); inverting silently
  invalidates that instruction.
- Do NOT change validation-finding filtering unless your design call covers both paths — they
  share filter_for_stdout/2.

Verification:
  mix test test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs test/mix/tasks/spec_tasks_test.exs
  mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix format --check-formatted
  mix spec.check --no-run-commands
  bash ./scripts/check_specs.sh
Those two files are the only ones carrying check_verbose_flag / branch_findings_breakdown tags.
No stub to flip.

Expected diff: ~60-110 lines across 4-6 files.

IMPLEMENTED
Session: i4x-bg5.5
Log: /Users/mz/.local/state/agentic-runs/specled_ex/specled_-bg5.5/codex-i4x-bg5.5/log

Files touched: .spec/decisions/specled.decision.self_authorized_info_stdout_carveout.md, .spec/specs/mix_tasks.spec.md, lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex, test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs
Tests added: Mix.Tasks.Spec.CheckTest — default run prints self-authorized weakening info details
Verification stubs flipped: none
Verification tier: change-scoped — mix compile --warnings-as-errors; mix test test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs test/mix/tasks/spec_tasks_test.exs; mix test --stale; mix format --check-formatted; mix spec.check --no-run-commands; full-system proof deferred to the merge gate / PR CI
Final-tier runs: 1

Summary: Default mix spec.check output now retains the append_only/self_authorized_weakening detail line while continuing to suppress every other informational finding unless verbose output is enabled. The spec amendment and adds-exception ADR record the held design decision, and an end-to-end Git fixture proves the real same-diff authorization path remains visible without becoming blocking.

VERIFY: PASS
Session: 9a42db78-611e-4632-882a-adaefdaa666f
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-specled-ex/9a42db78-611e-4632-882a-adaefdaa666f.jsonl

Mechanical checks:
- Files touched: 4 (.spec/decisions/specled.decision.self_authorized_info_stdout_carveout.md,
  .spec/specs/mix_tasks.spec.md, lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex, test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs)
  +175/-5, within the ~60-110 line expectation once the 62-line ADR is accounted for.
- Outside Allowed globs: 0
- branch_check.ex / severity.ex / append_only.ex / review/html.ex untouched: confirmed
  (git diff --name-only names none of them; realization_hashes.json also untouched and no
  drift finding fired, matching the contract's post-0.14.0 prediction for a run/1 body edit).

Semantic checks:
- Summary line format unchanged: verified by execution against a purpose-built git fixture,
  run once from this HEAD and once from the base checkout (bb64e69e). Both emit byte-identical:
    branch base=a3f5fff... changed_files=2 findings=1 (error=0 warning=0 info=1, info hidden; --verbose to show)
  The repo's own run is likewise unchanged in shape:
    branch base=origin/main changed_files=4 findings=3 (error=0 warning=0 info=3, info hidden; --verbose to show)
  No edit to print_branch_report/2; the diff touches only filter_for_stdout/2 and adds two
  private predicates.
- Carve-out is narrow (other :info codes still suppressed): confirmed two ways by execution.
  (1) mix spec.check --no-run-commands against THIS diff reports info=3 and prints ZERO [INFO]
      detail lines by default; --verbose reveals all three are branch_guard_missing_subject_update.
  (2) The pre-existing test "default run suppresses :info branch findings" (append_only/no_baseline)
      still passes unmodified. Implementation is a per-finding Enum.reject against a one-element
      code whitelist (@always_visible_info_codes = ["append_only/self_authorized_weakening"]),
      matched on code not message, so no severity-wide unsuppression is possible.
- Severity still :info and exit code still 0 with only that finding: confirmed by execution.
  append_only.ex:523-540 is untouched and still emits severity: :info. Built an isolated fixture
  where self_authorized_weakening is the ONLY finding (ADR affects: [billing.invoice,
  billing.receipt] with only invoice weakened, so same_pr_self_authorization does not co-fire).
  Bare default `mix spec.check --root <fixture> --base <base>` printed:
    [INFO] append_only/self_authorized_weakening - :: Weakening of `billing.invoice` (requirement
    deleted) is suppressed as authorized by ADR `billing.decision.retire_invoice` ...
    spec.check result=pass
  and the shell exit code was 0. The same fixture run from the base checkout prints the identical
  summary line with NO detail line and also exits 0 — so the diff adds visibility and changes
  nothing about exit-status math.
- --verbose still not the default: confirmed. verbose?/1 is untouched; the default repo run
  suppressed all 3 ordinary :info findings and printed "info hidden; --verbose to show", while
  --verbose printed all 3. The specled.package instruction to probe detector_unavailable with
  --verbose remains valid.
- Spec amendment + ADR: the ADR carries change_type: adds-exception and
  affects: [specled.tasks.check_verbose_flag] — exactly the amended requirement. It is registered
  in mix_tasks.spec.md's decisions: list. The must retains its shall-modal and priority: must; the
  amendment inserts "except `append_only/self_authorized_weakening`, whose detail line shall remain
  visible". A new scenario specled.tasks.check_verbose_flag.self_authorized_marker_visible covers it
  (scenario count for the requirement goes up, not down).
- append_only findings against THIS diff: NONE. `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` reports
  findings=3, all `branch_guard_missing_subject_update` at :info; zero append_only/* of any code.
  So this is NOT in practice the same-PR self-authorization case — no weakening was detected, and
  no authorization lookup consulted the new ADR. Reason: detect_must_downgraded
  (append_only.ex:164-190) keys on ModalClass of the statement, and the amended statement keeps
  "shall" throughout; deletion/polarity/scenario-regression detectors likewise do not fire on an
  in-place statement qualification. The ADR is therefore belt-and-braces rather than detector-
  mandated — the conservative and correct call, since the prose absolute really was removed from a
  must even though the mechanical detector is blind to it.
- Test drives real spec.check output, not a constructed finding map: confirmed. The new test builds
  a real git repo (init_git_repo, indexed + committed baseline state.json, second commit deleting a
  must plus a same-diff ADR), then calls Mix.Tasks.Spec.Check.run/1 and asserts on drained
  Mix.shell messages. The finding is produced by production branch enforcement, not fabricated. It
  asserts both halves: the unchanged summary line AND an [INFO] line containing the code, the
  weakened requirement id, and the authorizing ADR id. I independently reproduced the same path
  outside ExUnit via the CLI (above), which also exercises the real process exit code.
- Targeted verification (all from the stage worktree):
    MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors -> clean
    mix test test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs test/mix/tasks/spec_tasks_test.exs -> 45 tests, 0 failures
    mix format --check-formatted -> exit 0
    mix spec.check --no-run-commands -> spec.check result=pass, exit 0
  (An unrelated "./bin/sh: /var/.../specled_cmd_*.sh: No such file or directory" line appears in the
  test run; it comes from the untouched CheckCommandTimeoutTest 1ms-timeout fixture, not this diff.)
- Full-suite verification: not run by verifier (by design)

Verdict: PASS

Notes (advisory only):
- Cosmetic tension the contract forces and the ADR already acknowledges: when the only finding is
  the carve-out, the summary still reads "info hidden; --verbose to show" immediately above a
  printed [INFO] line. Correct per the do-not-change-the-summary constraint, and the ADR states the
  summary "continues to describe the bulk info-detail mode" — worth a follow-up ticket only if the
  wording ever confuses an adopter.
- No CHANGELOG.md entry. It was allowed but not required by the contract; flagging in case the
  release PR expects one.
- The carve-out lives in the shared filter, so it applies to validation findings too if that code
  ever surfaces there. The ADR calls this out deliberately; no action.

title: F25: :info findings invisible on default CLI output — self-auth marker only visible with --debug/HTML
